title: Abstract DP168: Chronic Stroke Plasma Triggers Microglial Activation and Cognitive Decline in Young Mice

evidence_spans.quote: Results: Mice infused with chronic stroke plasma exhibited impairments in recognition memory
male and female C57Bl/6 mice
Increased gliosis and senescent-like phenotypes were confirmed
Our ongoing work aims to identify the molecular mediators of these effects through multi-omic profiling.

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This is an empirical mouse study that measures senescence-associated markers and confirms senescent-like phenotypes. Multi-omic profiling is described only as ongoing future work, not as part of the current report.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Retro-orbital infusion of plasma from aged mice 6 months after transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (chronic stroke plasma)
causal_design_reviewer.comparator: Plasma from aged sham-surgery donor mice
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Recipient-mouse recognition and associative memory, microglial activation, cytokine production, mitochondrial activity, and senescence-related markers
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes in young recipients infused with chronic stroke plasma versus sham-donor plasma

evidence_spans.quote: Mice infused with chronic stroke plasma exhibited impairments in recognition memory (NORT) and associative memory (FCT)

delivered retro-orbitally into young (12-week-old) sex-matched C57Bl/6 recipients
